analysis.title: The 720: Panasonic, Mitsubishi Electric, Global DCs, Korea Financials, Komatsu, Delta Electronics, S-Oil, Hitachi, LVMH
key_insights: Panasonic HD (Buy on CL, 12m TP ¥6,300): 2Q FY3/26 results led to a 20% upward revision of full-year adjusted operating profit guidance, from ¥650bn to ¥780bn. Profitability is improving from AI-related industry products and from price hikes and structural reforms in Electric Works and Home Appliances.

Panasonic HD: GS expects ROIC focus and working capital improvements to lift free cash flow as investments in automotive batteries and Blue Yonder peak. Upside could come from higher utilization at the Kansas battery plant and resilient data center demand.

Mitsubishi Electric (Buy, 12m TP ¥7,400): full-year adjusted operating profit guidance was raised 15% to ¥710bn. Management expects non-AI demand to sustain Factory Automation momentum through FY3/28, with capacity expansion and margin gains in energy systems and defense.

Mitsubishi Electric: the planned deconsolidation of the automotive equipment business is expected to bring about ¥200bn in cash inflows, which GS expects to speed up ROE improvement and support shareholder returns.

Long-term rates: GS Global Markets attributes recent upward pressure on long-term rates mainly to the Fed's shift to a new hiking cycle rather than structural macro shocks. Forward yields above the last cycle's 5.3% peak would be unusual unless markets expect the Fed to exceed that level.

Long-term rates: GS says deep forward rates above 5% look less plausible if the funds rate peaks near its 4-4.25% modal forecast, though fiscal deficits and AI investment demand support a higher underlying rate structure.

Global data centers: GS raises its 2030 global capacity forecast to 273GW from 217GW, or 170GW of additional post-2025 capacity and $8.5tn of implied cumulative capex over five years. The revision comes from larger outer-year estimates for unannounced projects and fast neocloud additions. The US is expected to reach 152GW by 2030.

Global data centers: GS flags rising execution risks from power supply constraints, regulatory uncertainty and high leverage, but still sees outsized growth through projects with high power visibility.

Korea Financials: after a US marketing trip, GS says the bank share correction has overshot the temporary fundamental softness it anticipated. In GS's view the market is treating recent NIM weakness as permanent when the drivers were transitory. Samsung Life drew the most insurance questions after its hybrid issuance.

Komatsu (Buy, 12m TP ¥9,000 unchanged): a 2Q margin miss came from temporary one-off costs and timing mismatches. GS trims its FY3/27 operating profit estimate by 1% and keeps FY3/28 at ¥700bn. North American rental demand tied to AI and data center investment and copper and gold mining inquiries support growth.

Delta Electronics (Buy, 12m TP NT$4,120): 3Q26 missed because a 2pp inventory write-off hit gross margin. Management expects sequential recovery in 4Q26. AI-related revenue is above 50% of sales, and the board approved a new large production site in Malaysia. GS cuts 2026 and 2027 EPS estimates by 3% and sees HVDC power racks as a key profit driver.

S-Oil (Buy on CL): 12m TP cut to W210,000 from W220,000 after a 3Q operating profit that beat consensus by 10% on record lubricant earnings. GS cuts 2026E core EBITDA by 9.1%. Management expects tight refining conditions into 2027 and calls freight risk manageable with 65% term charter coverage. GS estimates a 26% free cash flow yield in 2027 after a 24% stock correction.

China Consumer Durables: covered white goods companies saw aggregate 3Q26 revenue down 7% and core net profit down 23% year-over-year. Gree and Hisense were hit hardest, while Midea and Haier were in line on overseas growth. GS expects 4% sector growth in 4Q26. Midea is preferred (Buy), Haier is Buy and Gree is Neutral.

China Spirits: Moutai and King's Luck outperformed while most peers focus on inventory digestion. GS cuts Wuliangye 2026E-28E sales estimates by 8%-9% and earnings forecasts by 9%-13%, with a 12m TP cut to Rmb59.2.

AMEC (Buy): 12m TP cut to Rmb500 from Rmb582. 3Q26 gross margin improved to 41.7% but revenue missed GS estimates by 25% on tight component supply. GS cuts 2026-28E revenue by 10%/2%/2% and 2027-28E net income by 7%/6%, while raising 2026E net income 4%.

China Solar: GS reiterates Sell on Daqo ADR, Daqo A and Tongwei. Daqo ADR missed with a US$53mn net loss on weak ASPs. GS expects 4Q26 shipments to fall 30% sequentially with flat ASPs, and is skeptical of the joint industry price hikes.

Marico (Buy, 12m TP Rs950): 2QFY27 EBITDA beat, with EBITDA up 27% as a 600bp gross margin expansion offset a 44% surge in advertising spend. Management upgraded FY27 EBITDA growth guidance to about 25% y/y. Domestic volume grew 10%.

Mitsui OSK Lines (Buy, 12m TP ¥7,800): FY3/27 operating profit guidance raised to ¥151bn from ¥135bn and recurring profit to ¥295bn from ¥225bn. GS sees the implied 2H outlook as conservative and sees potential for about ¥50bn of buybacks this fiscal year.

Hitachi (Buy, 12m TP ¥6,600): ahead of Hitachi Energy's Investor Day, the FY30 adjusted EBITA margin target was raised to 19-21% from 16-20% and the ROIC target to 30-40% from 25-30%. Management expects AI and digital utilization to add over US$350mn of profit per year.

Samsung F&M (Buy, 12m TP W860,000): management says the underwriting cycle is improving under a profit-first strategy. GS cites a sector-highest solvency ratio and a capital management framework targeting a 220% K-ICS.

Marvell announced a definitive all-stock agreement to acquire Lumentum (Not Rated). Management cites a combined 2030 TAM of about $550bn, including about $60bn incremental from NPO and CPO, and over $1bn of run-rate cost synergies, with non-GAAP EPS accretion one year after close.

Apple (Buy, 12m TP $390): F4Q26 beat with EPS of $2.10, revenue of $114.5bn and gross margin of 47.9%, on stronger iPhone and Mac revenue. GS expects F1Q27 guidance of low-to-mid single-digit revenue growth.

US Technology Hardware: GS is constructive on Dell, HPE and NetApp into C3Q26 results, raising EPS estimates by 5% (Dell F2027-29), 1% (HPE F2026-28) and 2% (NetApp F2027-28). GS stays bearish on HP and cuts its F2026-28 EPS estimates by 1%.

European Conviction List November update: Deutsche Bank and Carlsberg added, HSBC, Haleon and CTP removed. Deutsche Bank ROTE is forecast above 13% by 2028, with EPS 5-8% ahead of consensus. Carlsberg EPS is 2-4% ahead of consensus.

LVMH (Buy, 12m TP €495): GS cuts its Q4 Fashion & Leather organic growth estimate to -3% from -2% on China pressure but keeps +4% for FY27, citing Louis Vuitton stabilization, a Dior acceleration, and growth at Loro Piana and Rimowa.

market_movers.rationale: Panasonic HD: guidance for full-year adjusted operating profit raised 20% to ¥780bn on AI-related products and non-AI price hikes. Buy on conviction list.
Mitsubishi Electric: guidance raised 15% to ¥710bn, with broad-based demand and the automotive equipment deconsolidation worth about ¥200bn.
Komatsu: 2Q margin miss seen as temporary, FY3/28 operating profit forecast intact at ¥700bn.
Delta Electronics: 3Q26 miss from a 2pp inventory write-off hit to gross margin, with sequential recovery expected and AI above 50% of revenue.
S-Oil: TP cut from W220,000 after currency and working capital effects, despite a 10% 3Q operating profit beat. Buy on conviction list.
Midea is preferred in white goods for margin resilience and shareholder returns.
Haier is Buy on undemanding valuation.
Gree is Neutral on intensifying competition and market share loss.

AMEC: TP cut from Rmb582 after a 25% revenue miss versus GS estimates on tight component supply.
Daqo ADR: Sell reiterated. 3Q26 net loss of US$53mn on weak ASPs, with 4Q26 shipments expected to fall 30% sequentially.
Daqo A: Sell reiterated on weak price recovery, with the TP edged up to Rmb7.8.
Tongwei: Sell reiterated on cautious price recovery view, with the TP edged up to Rmb4.4.
Marico: 2QFY27 EBITDA beat with FY27 EBITDA growth guidance upgraded to about 25% y/y.
Mitsui OSK Lines: guidance raised on container shipping, with potential for about ¥50bn of buybacks.

Samsung F&M: profit-first strategy and improving underwriting cycle, with Value Up potential.

GS raises F2026-28 EPS by 1% on higher cloud and AI revenue.
GS raises F2027-28 EPS by 2% on higher ASPs and product revenue.
GS cuts F2026-28 EPS by 1% on softer PC unit volumes and a weaker print hardware backdrop.
